text:
tom_infra: Heads-up — we detected an intermittent GPU hardware fault on a Dedicated node in ap-south-1 tonight. Machine started reporting uncorrectable ECC/Xid errors and occasional process crashes around 22:10 UTC. We're planning to drain and swap the card under maintenance window on Monday. Drafting a short customer note below for feedback. :rotating_light:

maria_ops: Thanks for flagging. Can you paste the minimal logs we used to triage? Need concise, non-technical phrasing for customers plus an ops timeline. :thumbsup:

ashley_cs: I'll start a customer-friendly draft. Suggest we emphasize automatic failover (no data loss), expected downtime window for Dedicated nodes (hot-restart limited), and next steps for private deployments (on-prem tech contact required). Keep it empathetic and actionable.

liam_support: What's the exact impact on customer SLA and any potential rate limits while we shift workloads? We should include who to contact and an escalation path.

 tom_infra: Minimal logs below (scrubbed hostnames/IPs). Only include as internal reference, not for customers.

```
kernel: [ 12234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, Xid (00000000)
kern: [ 12234.567895] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has incurred an uncorrectable ECC error.
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,gpu_name,driver_version,retired_pages --format=csv
2026-03-15T22:09:01, A100-80GB, 535.XX, 0
2026-03-15T22:10:14, A100-80GB, 535.XX, 2
```

maria_ops: Ops plan (short): 1) mark node drained, 2) migrate active containers to standby pool, 3) queue physical card swap during maintenance Monday 06:00-09:00 UTC, 4) verification tests and bring back to rotation. Will keep customers on Dedicated notified with ETA updates.

ashley_cs: Draft customer-facing message (suggested):

"Hello — we wanted to let you know about a planned maintenance activity affecting a small number of Dedicated/Private GPU nodes in ap-south-1. Overnight monitoring detected a hardware fault on one GPU card. To keep your workloads running smoothly we will drain the affected node and failover workloads to redundant capacity. Physical replacement of the card is scheduled for Monday 06:00–09:00 UTC. You should not see data loss; some active jobs may restart during the failover. We will post live updates in this thread and reach out if any action is required from your side. Contact support@redwood.ai or reply to this message for questions or to request a business-impact review."

liam_support: That reads well. Add a line about SLA: "This maintenance is covered by our automated failover and does not count as downtime for dedicated throughput SLAs; if you do see persistent degradation please escalate."

maria_ops: Agree. Also include a brief note for Private on-prem customers: "If you're on an on-prem/private deployment, our field team will coordinate the physical replacement; expect a dedicated engineer call."
deploy-bot: autoscale: standby-pool scaled +3 nodes to absorb drained workloads (trigger: node-65 degraded)

ashley_cs: Final small edits and we'll send an outbound email + in-console banner. Add tracking link to support ticket and expected update cadence (every 30m until resolved).

customer-notify-bot: Outbound draft queued to mailing list for manual review by @ashley_cs and @maria_ops. Template: "Dedicated/Private GPU maintenance — ap-south-1 — card swap"

liam_support: I'll prepare the SLA note and escalation contact list. Maria, can you confirm whether there are any customers pinned to that physical host (reservation)? If yes, we need to call them directly.

maria_ops: Quick scan shows two Reserved Dedicated customers on that rack. I'll pull their contacts and ping them directly after we publish the general note.

tom_infra: I'll coordinate the replacement with on-call hardware vendor and post the replacement confirmation once complete. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
